comparison.summary: Your solution avoids sorting by scanning consecutive value groups; the existing Python solution sorts first.
details: Both keep the longest consecutive chain ending at each value and consider keeping x or increasing it to x + 1.
Your frequency map records real copies, possible contains x and x + 1, and each consecutive group starts only where the previous possible value is absent. Every actual copy is processed once.
Your update reads both previous DP states before writing either result. The existing Python writes dp[num + 1] before dp[num] to avoid reusing the same element.
Your expected time is O(n) with O(n) extra space. The existing Python uses sorted(nums), so its time is O(n log n) and its extra space is O(n). No JavaScript or TypeScript implementation was saved.

solutions.title: Frequency groups and dynamic programming
solutions.approach: No-sort version we ended on: frequency map, possible final-value set, and DP that processes each real copy.
